refreshes.notes: Nineteen minors, purely additive: 200 members -> 210, nothing withdrawn. The six changed operations all gained parameters — `metadata` on add_friends and create_api_friend, `joinRequired` on create_api_tournament, `party_update` on create_envelope_message, all optional; create_party_create_message and create_party_message gained `label`/`hidden` as required. The go/no-go verdict is unmoved: decision stays no-go and the missing-member set (12 API* enum constants plus six client-lifecycle names) is byte-identical to the v3.21.1 measurement, so the additions expand the emitted surface without covering anything the authored fork owns. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (830 type tokens, 0 unknown), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. The fragile `proto` source path into upstream's Go vendor/ tree survived the bump and was re-verified at v3.40.0 before fetching. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history and nothing is committed between checkpoints, so 19 intermediate fetches would multiply the work without adding an isolation point. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose — the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two minors plus a patch (1.2.5 -> 1.3.1), net additive: 809 members -> 839, three withdrawn. The removals are one rework, not a deprecation: druid.instance._input_blacklist and _input_whitelist collapse into the single _input_filter field plus the new input_filter.blacklist/whitelist pair, and druid.scroll._on_mouse_hover went away with it. New public API arrives on progress (get_value/set_value), swipe (is_enabled/set_enabled), timer (set_value), rich_text (set_justify/is_justify), drag (add_drag_action/remove_drag_action/hover), data_list (refresh), input (get_text_visual) and the module function get_druid; the druid.button.style constants are now surfaced as fields. get_widget is the one changed signature - it gained a trailing optional template parameter, which moved the docs-site emitter-equivalence assertion with it. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged, and every annotationOverrides key still resolved against the new fixtures (applyAnnotationOverrides throws on an absent key, so the emit pass proves it). staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so intermediate fetches would add work without an isolation point. Pinned at tag 1.3.1 rather than the 1.3.0 release because upstream:library-check ranks tags by commit date and 1.3.1 is the newest. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. A member present at BOTH refs but listed under addedMembers would pass, because the 1.2.5 fixture bytes do not survive this commit. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two majors (4 -> 6), the largest jump in this backlog: 135 members -> 153, two withdrawn, and both withdrawals were emitted in the shipped .d.ts at 4, so both break a consumer call site. `decore.event_bus.process_all` is gone because upstream folded it into `process`, which now takes an entity-aware callback and returns LuaMultiReturn<[events, entities]> instead of one list; `system.nocache` is gone with the tiny-ecs rework that replaced the no-cache opt-out with a shape cache (tiny_ecs.setShapeValidation, tiny_ecs.bumpShapeCache, world.shapeGeneration, world.shapeSystems, entity.__shape, system.hasOnModify are its new surface). The event bus gained entity-parallel storage (event_entities, stash_entities, get_event_entities, get_stash_entities) and widened its keys from `string` to `string | Hash`; `get_events` also changed from a nullary `(): void` to `(event_name): unknown[] | undefined`, so the old declaration was wrong about its own arity. Elsewhere: a new `remove_component` module function, a trailing optional `out` buffer on find_entities and tiny_ecs.findEntities, per-phase system lists on `world` (systemsUpdate, systemsPreWrap, systemsPostWrap, systemsLateUpdate, systemsFixedUpdate, systemsOnModify) plus world.event and world.id_to_entity, and system.decore.register_with_parent. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 204 type tokens), so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. `--fetch` has no per-target filter and re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; only fixtures/luals/decore/ moved, which confirms the other twelve tag pins are byte-stable. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch at 5 would add work without an isolation point. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

Two tags (19 -> 21) for the smallest delta in this backlog: of the five committed fixture files only event/promise.lua moved, and the model surface went 61 members -> 62 with one addition and no withdrawal. The one addition is `promise.on_cancel`, which upstream promoted to a public field on the promise class. That promotion has a second half the guard cannot witness: the same release re-annotated `cancellation` as `---@field private`, so `isPublicField` now hides it and the shipped surface swapped `cancellation: promise_cancelled_context` for `on_cancel: event` in both generated/event.d.ts and api-doc/event.json. That breaks a consumer who read `my_promise.cancellation`; the replacement is `my_promise.on_cancel`, the same underlying event object upstream previously reached only through `cancellation.on_cancel`. `removedMembers` is empty by construction rather than by observation: buildTargetModel — the guard's member source — retains members of every visibility and only the emit, api-doc and fidelity passes apply isPublicField, so naming `promise.cancellation` here would red the guard against a member the model still yields. `promise:cancel()` also changed behavior without changing arity: a settled promise is now left as-is instead of running _cancel_promise(), and only pending descendants are rejected. Fidelity coverage stays 1 (0 unknown, 85 type tokens) and fidelity/event.json is byte-unchanged, so fidelity-floor.json is unchanged. `--fetch` has no per-target filter and re-downloaded all 13 LuaLS targets; only fixtures/luals/event/ moved, which confirms the other twelve tag pins are byte-stable. Tags are bare integers, so 21 was resolved as the highest integer rather than the highest string, where 9 would outrank it. staged=false: the fixtures are snapshots rather than a replayable history, so an intermediate fetch at 20 would add work without an isolation point. What this guard can witness is directional: a removedMembers name still emitted, or an addedMembers name not emitted at all. changedMembers and these notes are unchecked prose - the committed guard reads addedMembers and removedMembers only.

deliberatelyUnmoved.reason: Examined during this refresh and deliberately left alone. The upstream default branch is one commit ahead of the pinned SHA and that commit touches README.md only, which no target consumes - so the pin is already correct and moving it would be churn on the most expensive lane. Re-verified at refresh time via the compare API.
